body.statement: If \(G=B=C=1\), then \(r_\ell^-=r_\ell^+=p_\ell\), \(t_\ell^-=t_\ell^+=p_\ell\), \(h^-=h^+=q_0\), and \(F_-(P)=F_+(P)=a\sum_{\ell=0}^1q_\ell p_\ell+(1-a)\sum_{\ell=0}^1q_\ell p_\ell=\sum_{\ell=0}^1q_\ell p_\ell\), the usual two-period g-formula with degenerate baseline for \(\mu_{11}\).
body.justification: The reduction verifies that the frontier nests the standard identified analysis when every sensitivity ratio is one.
body.gap: This is a required sanity reduction, not a novelty claim beyond Tan's sensitivity-free model.
body.consumer: It lets an implementation recover the ordinary sustained-treatment risk as a unit test.
body.proof_tex:
When \(K=1\), the definitions give \(D_1(x)=U_1(x)=x\).  Therefore \(G=B=C=1\) implies, for each \(\ell\),
\[
 r_\ell^-=r_\ell^+=e_\ell p_\ell+(1-e_\ell)p_\ell=p_\ell,\qquad
 t_\ell^-=t_\ell^+=p_\ell,\qquad h^-=h^+=q_0.
\]
Substitution into either compact endpoint gives
\[
 F_-(P)=F_+(P)
 =a\sum_{\ell=0}^1q_\ell p_\ell
 +(1-a)\{q_0p_0+q_1p_1\}
 =\sum_{\ell=0}^1q_\ell p_\ell.
\]
By the sharp-frontier theorem, the causal identified set is the singleton containing this observed-law functional.  Under the two consistency assumptions it is precisely the ordinary two-period g-formula for \(\mu_{11}\), completing the sanity reduction.
